Here's a recipe that my girlfriend and I enjoy cooking. The sauce recipe is meant for 16oz of chicken breast, but can lightly cover up to 20oz. We typically combine this with either a simple fried rice or white rice recipe.

For the baked chicken:

  • 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into small 1-inch chunks
  • Salt and pepper to taste; experiment with other spices if you're feeling adventurous
  • 2 large eggs, beaten
  • 1 cup Panko Japanese bread crumbs

For the delicious, delicious sauce:

  • 1/3 cup honey (more to taste if you'd like, but I'd start with the recommended amount)
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced (or 1 tsp garlic powder)
  • 2 tablespoons soy sauce
  • 1 tablespoon Sriracha (I like this for the added kick)
  • 1 tablespoon cornstarch
  • 2 green onions, thinly sliced
  • 2 teaspoons sesame seeds INSTRUCTIONS

Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Lightly oil a 9x13 baking dish or coat with nonstick spray. Season chicken with salt and pepper, to taste. Dip the prepared chicken into eggs, then dredge in Panko, pressing to coat. This step can be messy if you're not used to dredging stuff in Panko. Add chicken to baking dish and place into oven and bake until golden brown and crisp. We usually give it about 15-20 minutes.

In a medium saucepan over medium-high heat, combine honey, garlic, soy sauce and Sriracha. In another small bowl, combine cornstarch and 1/3 cup water and mix together. Stir the cornstarch/water mixture into the saucepan containing the other ingredients until thickened,which usually takes 2-3 minutes. Stir in the chicken and gently toss (or stir) to combine. Garnish the dish with the green onions and sesame seeds if desired.

Get it while it's hot. Tastes great as leftovers too.
